proposals: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should notify final Battery Pack Aadhaar guidelines with a compliance date and penalties, and confirm in the notification whether they will be finalised through the AISC process, so the January 2026 draft becomes a rule with a known route.

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and CPCB should require that a battery's Battery Pack Aadhaar Number and its EPR barcode or QR code resolve to the same record, so each battery carries one identifier instead of separate codes for lifecycle tracking and waste accountability.

BIS should make the IS 16046 registration number, and PESO the facility licence number where one applies, mandatory fields in the Battery Pack Aadhaar record, so a single scan shows whether the cell was certified and where it was made or stored.

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should publish an annual register of electric-vehicle battery fire incidents by vehicle category, manufacturer and identified cause, so the effect of AIS-156's thermal-runaway rules after the 2022 fires can be measured with Indian data.

DGCA should publish an annual count of lithium-battery incidents on flights by Indian carriers, by device type, so the effect of its November 2025 power-bank advisory can be checked and India has its own transport-incident data rather than relying on global figures.
